questions.text: Citizen Data Access Logs: Knowing who viewed your data: (1) User portal to view access history ('Who checked my ID?'); (2) Notification of access; (3) Purpose of access declaration; (4) List of authorized agencies; (5) Dispute mechanism for unauthorized access; (6) Data sharing agreements publication; (7) Audit trail visibility.
questions.evidence_required: Portal screenshots, Access log samples, Data sharing MOUs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Citizens fear state surveillance. Seeing who accessed their data builds massive trust (e.g., Estonia model).

questions.text: Privacy Policy & Rights: Clear rules: (1) Plain language privacy policy; (2) Translation into local languages; (3) Disclosure of third-party processors; (4) Right to correction explanation; (5) Data retention policy disclosure; (6) Contact for privacy officer; (7) Consent management (for optional services).
questions.evidence_required: Privacy policy docs, Translation samples, Consent forms
questions.africa_specific_notes: Privacy policies often copy-pasted and ignored. Illiterate users need audio/visual explanations.

questions.text: ID System Procurement Transparency: Who built it?: (1) Open tender process; (2) Publication of contract awards; (3) Beneficial ownership of local partners; (4) Cost per card/registrant disclosure; (5) Vendor track record check; (6) Technology lock-in disclosure; (7) Source code ownership (Open Source?).
questions.evidence_required: Tender documents, Contract awards, Beneficial ownership registry
questions.africa_specific_notes: ID contracts are multi-million dollar deals prone to corruption. 'Secret' security contracts often hide kickbacks.

questions.text: Public Expenditure Tracking: Where the money goes: (1) Budget allocation for digital projects; (2) Expenditure reports; (3) Audit General reports on project; (4) Value for money assessment; (5) Donor funding transparency; (6) Recurring cost disclosure (license fees); (7) Public dashboard.
questions.evidence_required: Budget docs, Audit reports, Expenditure dashboards
questions.africa_specific_notes: Digital projects often have huge cost overruns. Public needs to know if loan money was used effectively.

questions.text: Official Fee Transparency: Preventing bribes: (1) Clear display of official fees (posters/online); (2) Digital payment only (no cash = no bribes); (3) Receipt generation; (4) 'Service Charter' (timelines); (5) Reporting channel for bribe demands; (6) Refund policy; (7) Fee breakdown.
questions.evidence_required: Fee schedule, Digital receipt samples, Service charter
questions.africa_specific_notes: Citizens often pay 'facilitation fees' to get IDs. Digital payments (Mobile Money) reduce this friction.

questions.text: Application Tracking & Status: Reducing uncertainty: (1) SMS/Online status tracking; (2) Clear rejection reasons; (3) Estimated completion date; (4) Notification of readiness; (5) Queue visibility (for physical centers); (6) Escalation for delays; (7) Lost application recovery.
questions.evidence_required: Tracking portal demo, SMS logs, Rejection letter templates
questions.africa_specific_notes: People travel long distances to check if ID is ready. SMS notification saves time and money.

questions.text: Automated Decision Transparency: Explaining algorithms: (1) Explanation of automated rejection (e.g., photo quality); (2) Criteria for 'flagging' suspicious applications; (3) Human-in-the-loop for final rejection; (4) Bias testing of algorithms; (5) Appeal process for automated decisions; (6) Source of data for verification; (7) Error rates disclosure.
questions.evidence_required: Algorithm documentation, Appeal process flow, Bias audit
questions.africa_specific_notes: Automated systems might flag certain names/regions as 'suspicious'. Transparency prevents discrimination.

questions.text: Open Data & Statistics: Public insights: (1) Publication of enrollment stats (by region/gender); (2) Service delivery stats; (3) API for researchers (anonymized); (4) Census data integration; (5) Timeliness of data; (6) Data quality reports; (7) Visualization dashboards.
questions.evidence_required: Open data portal, Statistical reports, API docs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Data often hidden. Open data helps private sector plan and civil society monitor inclusion.

scoring_notes: Layer 2 (Transparency) for Government in SSA: Transparency is the antidote to corruption. Knowing 'who accessed my data' and 'what is the official fee' changes the power dynamic.
